newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to auction 14.99 pct of Nafta-Moskva.
newsitem.headline: Russia to auction 14.99 pct of Nafta-Moskva.

text.p: Russia will sell 14.99 percent of oil trader OAO Nafta-Moskva at a commercial tender on April 9, the Federal Property Fund (RFFI) said on Monday.

The 124,401 share stake has a starting price of 71 billion roubles, and the winner must invest $6.0 million in the company over three years, it said in an advance copy of the latest edition of its bulletin Reforma.
The winner of the tender will make the $6.0 million investment through an oil export agreement with Nafta-Moskva, the fund said.

Under this agreement the winner must agree to export at least 12 million tonnes of oil over three years, at a rate of at least four million tonnes a year, paying Nafta-Moskva a commission of $0.50 a tonne.
Nafta-Moskva's authorised capital is 829.35 billion roubles, comprising 588,842 ordinary shares and 240,511 preferred shares, each with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles, and one golden share.
In January ZAO Svift Ltd, a previously unknown company, won a tender for 14 percent of Nafta-Moskva, or 116,110 shares, for 66.1 billion roubles, and a commitment to invest $2.7 million.

In 1995 Nafta-Moskva itself and Uninvest, a bank, backed by Uneximbank, won control of a 15 percent government stake in Nafta-Moskva under the government's shares-for-loans scheme, with a credit to the government of $20.1 million.
